question.text: What is the primary purpose of Customer Due Diligence (CDD) in the AML/CFT framework?

answer.text: To verify customer identity and understand the nature of their activities to assess money laundering risk
To determine the creditworthiness of a customer for lending purposes
To evaluate a customer's investment knowledge and experience
To assess the suitability of financial products for the customer

explanation.text: The Logic: CDD is the screening and verification of the customer using reliable and independent sources so that the customer is risk-assessed before onboarding. The CDD measures include client identification and verification, understanding the purpose and intended nature of the business relationship, identifying beneficial ownership and the ownership/control structure, ongoing scrutiny of transactions, and periodic updating of identification data. The Trap: Creditworthiness assessment is part of lending norms, and investor suitability assessment is part of the investment advice / product-suitability framework — neither is the purpose of CDD under the AML/CFT framework. Note: The CDD definition and the list of measures above are grounded in the checked Series XXIV workbook pages on CDD.
